newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Gulf grades edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Gulf grades edge higher.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer in outright terms on Wednesday, with a slightly firmer tone to Middle East grades.
At the same time, further deals concerning West African import emerged as the Brent/Dubai spread narrowed further owing to a strong Dubai market.
January Brent/Dubai was assessed at $1.78/$1.85 per barrel, in from a day-earlier $1.95/$2.00 which is likely to spark fresh interest for West African grades, traders said.
January/February Dubai spread firmed to 52/60 from 50/58 and February/March to 52/65 from 50/60.
Brokers said the strength of the Dubai market -- where wet premiums for January have risen to full month quotes plus 80 cents from plus mid 60s -- was behind weaker Brent/Dubai spread.
In the Gulf market, majors exchanged an Umm Shaif at ADNOC plus 71 cents and an Oman at MPM +15 cents.
A second Oman cargo was heard done at MPM +15 cents between Japanese players and a 300,000-barrel parcel was heard sold at MPM +13 cents by a Japanese trader to a U.S. major.
Elsewhere, two Qatar Land deals were heard but initial information was vague as price differences were QGPC plus 40 cents and QGPC plus 52 cents.

A French major is loading December Djeno and Forcados grades for a South Korean refiner and a Japanese refiner respectively. Price indications were vague, although the Forcados was heard done at dated Brent plus $2.00 on a delivered basis.
A cargo of Dec 8-10 Bras River was said fixed by a trader into a Pertamina affiliate at dated Brent plus 30 to 40 cents.

In regional crudes, a Japanese trader sold around 150,000 barrels of Belida at ICP flat into Japan. The previous deal was done at ICP plus 70 cents traders said, but the latest barrels had no flexibility on loading dates.
